name: Lesson 1 · Being and naming: sein, pronouns, der/die/das

cards.note: sein, present tense. sein is irregular in every person, so learn its forms as a set: ich bin.
sein, present tense. du bist: like most du forms it ends in -st, but sein changes its whole stem.
sein, present tense. er, sie and es all take ist.
sein, present tense. A noun as the subject takes the same form as er/sie/es: ist.
sein, present tense. wir sind — the same form serves sie (they) and Sie (formal you).
sein, present tense. ihr seid, with a d: not sind, which belongs to wir and sie.
sein, present tense. sie (they) takes sind, like wir.
sein, present tense. Formal Sie always takes sind, even when you speak to one person.

cards.front: The man and the woman **are** here.
cards.back: Der Mann und die Frau **sind** hier.
cards.note: sein, present tense. Two subjects joined by und are plural: sind.
sein, present tense. ja stands outside the sentence, so the verb is still second: ich bin.
sein, present tense. nein, like ja, does not count as a position: das Haus comes first, then ist.
Subject pronouns. ich is written lower-case unless it starts the sentence — unlike English I.
Subject pronouns. du is for one person you know well: a friend, family, a child.
Subject pronouns. sie with ist means she; the verb tells it apart from they.
Subject pronouns. wir: we.
Subject pronouns. ihr is du for several people at once.
Subject pronouns. sie with sind means they — only the verb shows it is not she.
Subject pronouns. Sie with a capital S is the polite you, for one person or several.
Subject pronouns. es stands for a das-word: das Buch → es.
der, die, das: every noun has a gender. der Mann is masculine. Always learn a noun together with its article.
der, die, das: every noun has a gender. die Frau is feminine.
der, die, das: every noun has a gender. das Kind is neuter: gender belongs to the word, not to the person.
der, die, das: every noun has a gender. der Hund: masculine.
der, die, das: every noun has a gender. die Katze: most nouns ending in -e are feminine.
der, die, das: every noun has a gender. das Haus: neuter. Das ist… points at anything — the second das is the article.
der, die, das: every noun has a gender. das Auto: nouns ending in -o are usually neuter.
der, die, das: every noun has a gender. das Buch: neuter.
der, die, das: every noun has a gender. der Tisch: masculine, though it is a thing — grammar, not meaning.
der, die, das: every noun has a gender. die Lampe: feminine, like most nouns in -e.
der, die, das: every noun has a gender. The subject takes the nominative: der Hund.
der, die, das: every noun has a gender. die Frau as the subject: nominative, unchanged.

cards.front: The table is new. **It** is very big.
cards.back: Der Tisch ist neu. **Er** ist sehr groß.
cards.note: er, sie, es for things. A der-word is er, even a thing: der Tisch → er.

cards.front: The lamp is old. **It** is small.
cards.back: Die Lampe ist alt. **Sie** ist klein.
cards.note: er, sie, es for things. A die-word is sie: die Lampe → sie.

cards.front: The car is new. **It** is big.
cards.back: Das Auto ist neu. **Es** ist groß.
cards.note: er, sie, es for things. A das-word is es: das Auto → es.

cards.front: The dog is old. **He** is tired.
cards.back: Der Hund ist alt. **Er** ist müde.
cards.note: er, sie, es for things. der Hund → er, as in English he for a pet.

cards.front: The child is tired. **It** is small.
cards.back: Das Kind ist müde. **Es** ist klein.
cards.note: er, sie, es for things. das Kind → es, whether the child is a boy or a girl.
